name: Fret Shed
tagline: Guitar practice built around the songs you want to play
about: Fret Shed builds practice sessions around the songs you want to play, decodes chord charts and strumming patterns, does the capo and transposition maths, and fixes buzzing, sore fingers and slow changes.
persona: You are a working guitar teacher: song-first, technique-honest, one fix at a time, and you always tell the student what tempo to practise at.

onboarding.title: Play the songs, not just the scales
onboarding.subtitle: Your guitar, level and goals shape every session.
bullets: Chord & strum help for any track

profile.label: Goal
profile.placeholder: play at a friend's wedding in June

tools.title: Practice session
tools.subtitle: Blocks, tempos and a done-when
tools.prompt: Plan a {minutes}-minute practice session around '{song}' with focus on {struggle} for the profile: table (Block | Minutes | Exercise | Tempo BPM | Done when), steps for the single technique fix that matters most, and a callout on when to stop before bad habits set in.

tools.title: Learn this song
tools.subtitle: Key, capo, chords per section, a week plan
tools.prompt: For '{track}' ({want}) at the profile level: kv (key, capo suggestion, tempo, time signature, difficulty /5), a table of the sections (Section | Chords | Strum or picking pattern | Tip), steps to learn it over one week, and a callout on the trickiest change with an easier voicing. Do not reproduce the lyrics.

tools.title: Capo & transpose
tools.subtitle: Same song, easier shapes or a better key
tools.prompt: Transpose {chords} to {why}, details: {detail}. Sections: a table (Capo fret | Shapes to play | Sounding chords | Comfort) with the 3 best options, text on which to pick and why, and bullets on capo placement so nothing buzzes or goes sharp.

tools.title: Fix my playing
tools.subtitle: Buzz, pain, slow changes, muted strings
tools.prompt: Diagnose {problem} (already tried: {context}) on the profile guitar: table (Likely cause | How to check | Fix), steps for a 5-minute daily drill, and a callout on when the problem is the guitar's setup (action, nut, strings) rather than the player.

tools.title: Fretboard theory
tools.subtitle: Understand it on the neck, not on paper
tools.prompt: Explain '{topic}' for the profile level using the guitar itself, not abstract theory: text in plain words, steps to hear and feel it on the fretboard in the next 5 minutes, a kv of the 3 shapes or positions to memorise, and a quote with a one-line memory hook.

disclaimer: Practice guidance only, not medical advice; stop for sharp or persistent pain and see a clinician.
